verdicts.quote: View all data that fastfetch detects:
verdicts.diagnosis: The instruction promises all detected data while the command selects particular modules.
verdicts.evidence: Line 100 requires module selections through -s; line 181 demonstrates JSON output for only os. Line 99 separately provides the all-supported-modules command.
verdicts.deletion_test: Narrow the scope of 'all data' to the selected modules while preserving the command.

verdicts.reason: This describes the linked generator's functionality. The source identifies no omitted options or conflicting limitation; requiring a coverage account would demand implementation proof.

The page links a benchmark and states a performance focus. It supplies no conflicting result or narrower benchmark conditions; the absence of reproduced measurements alone does not establish a useful correction.
The default-module limitation is explicit and does not contradict the feature-total claim. Missing comparative counts alone do not establish an overstatement.

The README describes several configuration mechanisms and links further documentation. It establishes no conflicting limitation; requiring a Neofetch configuration inventory would add a proof requirement.

verdicts.diagnosis: The general superiority claim exceeds the specific output-formatting distinction offered as its basis.
verdicts.evidence: Line 123 compares only Memory and Disk output, including decimal precision and unit labels. Those examples support a formatting distinction rather than overall polish.
verdicts.deletion_test: Narrow the comparison to the illustrated formatting choices while retaining the examples and values.

verdicts.diagnosis: The unrestricted accuracy comparison generalizes beyond the particular detection and counting cases described.
verdicts.evidence: Line 124 cites Wayland support; lines 203–204 identify specific package-count errors. These establish particular comparison points, not a general accuracy ranking.
verdicts.deletion_test: Limit the accuracy comparison to the documented cases, preserving the Wayland link and package-count explanations.

verdicts.quote: A local IP address (10.x.x.x, 172.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) has nothing to do with privacy.
verdicts.diagnosis: The categorical privacy dismissal exceeds the networking explanation supplied.
verdicts.evidence: Lines 128–130 explain same-network use and SSH convenience. Line 311 separately addresses network transmission under an explicit condition; neither establishes that displaying an address has no privacy implications.
verdicts.source_function: Privacy reassurance about displayed local addresses.
verdicts.deletion_test: Remove the categorical absence-of-privacy claim or narrow it to the networking scope actually explained, preserving the address examples.

verdicts.quote: It only has meaning if you are on the same network, for example, if you connect to the same Wi-Fi network.
verdicts.diagnosis: The sentence treats a described networking use as an exclusive condition for the address having any meaning.
verdicts.evidence: Line 130 illustrates using addresses to SSH into test VMs. That practical use supports the network explanation but not the broader exclusion of informational meaning outside that setting.
verdicts.deletion_test: Narrow the exclusivity to the described networking use while preserving the same-network condition and Wi-Fi example.

verdicts.reason: 'Usually' already qualifies the troubleshooting observation. The following text identifies a concrete incompatibility and initialization remedy; missing frequency statistics alone do not justify correction.
In context, this describes an explicit override for Fastfetch's output mode. It does not promise to fix every terminal problem, and the source supplies no exception to the override's stated behavior.

The assurance explicitly excepts user- or operator-requested activity. The warning about executing untrusted configurations does not establish a transfer outside that condition; missing network-control implementation details are insufficient.
